slides.title: Today, and where it goes
slides.presenterNote: ≈ 2 min, and the first thing cut when time runs short. If under a minute: say only bullets 3 and 4 — clear flags by assigning a mask, the RM's access type tells you which polarity; an interrupt is a function call hardware makes — DIER raises it, the NVIC admits it, the vector table names it. Everything else is in the book. Do not run past the hour to finish this slide.
items: A timer is rate times count: prescaler and auto-reload, each written minus one, each 16 bits.
Five writes to start it; after that the hardware needs nothing from the CPU.
Status flags clear by assigning a mask — and the access type in the RM says which type.
An interrupt is a function call hardware makes: DIER raises it, the NVIC admits it, the vector table names it.
Anything an ISR shares with main needs to be volatile, and ISRs need to stay short.
